newsitem.title: UK: New UK industry pollution controls seen in 1997.
newsitem.headline: New UK industry pollution controls seen in 1997.

text.p: New environmental controls on British industry are expected to be published in the summer of 1997, the organisers of a consultation meeting on the plans said on Thursday.

Zeneca Group Plc's Environmental Laboratory, which specialises in testing toxic effluent from factories, said it had brought together representatives from more than 70 British companies to thrash out proposals put forward by the government-sponsored Environment Agency (EA).

The EA, which resulted from the merger of the National Rivers Authority and the government's pollution inspectorate, wants to introduce more sophisticated ways of assessing environmental damage caused by waste products from factories and sewerage plants.
Under the plans effluent would be assessed on its impact as a whole rather than broken down into component parts as at present.

Fiona Russell, environment executive of the Chemical Industries Association, said industry would be working with agency to find the best ways of using new evaluation techniques "in a cost effective manner."
The cost of the new recommendations has been a major concern for some companies who fear it will be more expensive than existing measurements.
